summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint into two lanes: reference copper producers with material SX-EW or acid integration, and underfollowed public acid/sulphur-chain names whose relevance may be hidden by chemical-logistics or junior-miner labels. The strongest direct exposure in this pass is not AI or battery OEMs, but copper leach operators, smelter-acid producers, and sulphuric-acid logistics/producers. Key uncertainty: whether the 2026 acid/sulphur disruption is temporary trade-route stress or a durable structural constraint that changes realized margins, customer behavior, or project economics. Layer 1B expansion found a thin US-listed universe with direct or second-order exposure to the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint. The cleanest underfollowed lane candidates are Hawkins as a US industrial-chemical distributor that explicitly handles sulfuric acid, and Ardmore Shipping as a small-cap product/chemical tanker operator that could be exposed to rerouted chemical/acid flows. Reference anchors are Freeport-McMoRan and Southern Copper: both are large copper producers tied to SX-EW/leaching and sulfuric-acid integration, but they are included mainly to map demand sensitivity and internal byproduct-acid offsets rather than as obscure alpha candidates. Several more direct acid assets appear private, foreign-listed, or OTC-only, creating a coverage gap for later passes.
